question: Compare CSCI-UA 201, CSCI-UA 202, and CSCI-UA 310.

# Comparison of CSCI-UA 201, CSCI-UA 202, and CSCI-UA 310

## Content Focus

**[CSCI-UA 201]** (Computer Systems Organization) covers the internal structure of computers, machine (assembly) language programming, and pointers in high-level languages. **[CSCI-UA 310]** (Basic Algorithms) is distinct in focus from the other two, centering on designing data structures and analyzing algorithm efficiency. - **[CSCI-UA 201]** requires CSCI-UA 102 OR CSCI-SHU 210 OR CS-UH 1050 (with a minimum grade of C, or equivalent A Level/IB scores).
- **[CSCI-UA 202]** requires CSCI-UA 201 (minimum grade C) OR equivalent courses (CENG-SHU 202, CS-UH 2010, ENGR-UH 3511) — meaning **[CSCI-UA 202] builds directly on [CSCI-UA 201]**, forming a sequence.
- **[CSCI-UA 310]** has a different prerequisite chain entirely: CSCI-UA 102 (minimum grade C) AND MATH-UA 120 (minimum grade C) AND (MATH-UA 121 OR MATH-UA 131 or equivalent). This ties **[CSCI-UA 310]** to math coursework (calculus) rather than to [CSCI-UA 201] or [CSCI-UA 202], indicating it does not depend on systems knowledge from those two courses.

## Summary of Relationship

[CSCI-UA 201] and [CSCI-UA 202] form a direct prerequisite sequence focused on systems-level topics (architecture → operating systems), both involving hands-on programming. [CSCI-UA 310] is a separate track requiring only introductory programming (CSCI-UA 102) plus calculus, and focuses on algorithmic/data-structure theory rather than systems programming, with homework not necessarily requiring code.
